title: controlplane-egress-service-chain-and-dns-failover-orchestrator
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Production control planes deployed into customer VPCs (Private) sometimes observe intermittent egress path failure when primary privatelink proxies are overloaded or when subnet affinity causes cross-AZ transient connectivity issues. This PR introduces a composable 'egress service chain' abstraction plus Route53-based DNS failover stitching to provide deterministic fallback paths, safer upgrades, and clearer observability for controlplane outbound traffic.

What this implements: a) Terraform: a new module 'egress_service_chain' that models an ordered list of egress targets (Privatelink endpoint -> zonal proxy NLB -> regional egress proxy -> S3/VPC endpoint) with conditional route table attachments and cross-account IAM roles required for peering/bind operations; b) Helm values & templates: new chart values for the installer and controlplane charts (private-controlplane.egress.serviceChain) allowing operators to declare the chain at install/upgrade time and opt into staged rollout; c) DNS failover: Route53 health checks + failover/weighted records wired to alias records for NLBs and privatelink endpoints to ensure sub-30s automatic switchover when a target becomes unhealthy; d) Security: SG templates and least-privilege IAM role bindings for the chain components and a new egress-sg preflight validator; e) Rollout tooling: a CLI hook in the installer that performs a canary swap and verifies healthchecks before applying route changes.

Files changed (high level): updated terraform modules (modules/egress_service_chain/*), hooks in installer/terraform/live/bootstrap.tf, helm charts (charts/private-controlplane/values.schema.yaml, templates/egress-chain-configmap.yaml), add e2e smoke test (test/egress_chain_smoke.sh), and docs (docs/private-deploy/egress-service-chain.md).

Migration and rollout: default behavior is backwards-compatible: service chain is opt-in via helm values. Existing deployments are unaffected until operator explicitly updates values or runs the installer hook. For customers who enable the module, the installer performs a preflight check that validates route table ownership, CIDR non-overlap, and presence of required privatelink endpoints. The canary procedure updates a per-az route attachment for 5% of controlplane traffic (via routing weight/target group attachment), monitors latency/error budgets for 15 minutes, and automatically rolls back if healthchecks trip.

Testing and verification: ran full terraform plan/apply in staging (account-stg-3), smoke tests against NLB failover scenarios (simulate target failure by deregistering target), Route53 failover verification, and added new unit tests for the terraform module's input validation. Integration pipeline initially failed on a flaky import test (terraform import of existing endpoint) — fixed by adding an import helper and retry logic; CI was re-run and passed.

Security considerations: tightened egress SGs to only allow outbound to specific privatelink and NLB ranges, added IAM role with scoped AssumeRole for cross-account peering operations, and added audit log entries for route modifications. No secrets were added; all new infra accepts existing KMS keys and follows account-bound policies.

Performance and cost: the default chain adds an NLB per-az when enabled which increases hourly infra cost moderately; however the chain enables more efficient local failover and reduces expensive cross-AZ proxy hop latencies in failure scenarios. See perf_impact below for numbers from staging.

Release notes: Adds opt-in controlplane egress service chaining with automated DNS failover and safe canary rollout. Operators must opt-in and may need to grant cross-account role for peering automation.

Related: ENG-3248 (egress stability), ENG-3301 (installer hooks), SUP-2124 (customer incident that motivated deterministic failover).

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Please tighten the security group egress CIDR to the minimum set of privatelink/NLB ranges and add comments explaining the sources; also add an explicit deny for 0.0.0.0/0 where not required.
Aisha Patel: Addressed — updated modules/networking/sg-templates/egress-sg.tf with narrower egress ranges, added inline comments and a configurable extra_allowed_cidrs parameter (default empty).
Priya Narang: Request changes — add terraform import tests and make the module idempotent against pre-existing endpoints; integration pipelines failed on this previously.
Aisha Patel: Added ci/integration/terraform-import-helper.sh and retry logic; updated module to use data sources when endpoints exist. Pushed commit f9c8e12 to address flakiness.
Lena Schmidt: Approved after verification on staging and confirming preflight checks — left a 👍
Ethan Cole: Approved — I re-ran the integration suite and confirmed no regressions in installer bootstrapping.
release_notes: Opt-in egress service chaining for private controlplane deployments: deterministic failover via Route53 health checks, installer canary hook, new Terraform module, tightened egress SGs. Operators must opt in and may need to grant a cross-account role for peering automation.
upgrade_instructions: Default: no change. To enable, add 'privateControlPlane: { egress: { serviceChain: enabled } }' to your installer values.yaml and provide cross-account role ARN via 'egress.serviceChain.crossAccountRoleArn'. Run 'installer apply --canary' to perform a staged rollout. See docs/private-deploy/egress-service-chain.md for full checklist.
testing_summary: Staging (account-stg-3): terraform plan/apply, smoke test (simulate NLB target failure), Route53 failover observed <25s to fallback target. Integration pipeline initially failed due to terraform import flake; fixed and re-run. Unit tests for input validation added and passing.
perf_impact: Staging numbers: median egress latency during failover reduced from 420ms to 110ms when chain is enabled (local zonal NLB fallback) at cost of ~0.09 USD/hr per additional NLB per AZ. Exact numbers depend on topology.
security_review: SRE and Security reviewed SG tightening and IAM scope; added audit events for route modifications and require operator-managed KMS for any NLB certificates. No PII exfiltration risk introduced by this change.
